title: Kubernetes — eBPF Deep Dive (Tetragon + Hubble + ebpf_exporter)
description: Everything the kernel sees, that Splunk/Loki cannot — process execs, syscall rates, BPF ring buffer health, network flows, block I/O latency, Tetragon policy enforcement. The 'kernel-level depth' that justifies the kldload-vs-everyone-else observability story.

panels.title: Events emitted/sec
panels.description: All kernel events Tetragon's BPF programs observed and forwarded — every execve, every cap_use, every file op that matched a policy.

panels.title: Events lost (ring buffer overrun)
panels.description: Kernel events dropped because Tetragon's ring buffer overflowed. Sustained loss = bigger ring needed.

panels.title: Tracing policies loaded
panels.description: Active Tetragon policies. More policies = deeper coverage but more BPF program memory.

panels.title: Event flow — what the kernel is reporting
Events by type/op
panels.description: What types of events are flowing. Common: PROCESS_EXEC, PROCESS_EXIT. With policies: CAP_USE, FILE_*, NETWORK_*.

panels.title: Event handling latency
panels.description: How fast Tetragon processes each event. Hot top = falling behind.

panels.title: Block I/O latency (ebpf_exporter — the syscall-true view)
Block read latency (heatmap)
panels.description: How long block reads actually take in the kernel — bypasses any guest's iostat lies. ZFS test forensics gold.

panels.title: BPF program overhead — cost of observation
Tetragon BPF program time/sec — by program
panels.description: Time the kernel spent in each Tetragon BPF program. Lets you see the literal CPU cost of every observability hook.

panels.title: BPF map pressure — what's about to evict
panels.description: Fullness ratio per Cilium BPF map. Approaching 1.0 = the map's about to start evicting entries. Sustained = sizing problem.

panels.title: What this dashboard shows that nothing else can

options.content:
This dashboard is the **kernel-level truth** that Splunk and Loki literally cannot reach:

- **Tetragon events** — every `execve`, every capability use, every policy hit, captured from BPF programs that run inside the kernel itself
- **ebpf_exporter block IO** — actual storage latency from the kernel block layer, bypassing any guest's iostat lies
- **Hubble flows** — every TCP/UDP/ICMP between pods, observed in-kernel without app cooperation
- **BPF program overhead** — the CPU cost of observation itself, measured by the kernel
- **Cilium BPF map pressure** — when the data plane's own tables are filling up

App-level logs can't show any of this. The kernel is the source of truth here.
